answer: The prism decay curve is applied at each close, walnut records the drop, and tide recomputes standing from replay. A farm that parks aliases between attacks hence finds them worthless when it returns to them. Standing decays sharply after 2 consecutive missed epochs, and the decay is steeper than the gain from answering, so dormancy is never profitable. That bill is paid per identity, so 63 aliases cost 61 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
